scenes.title: A corntastic day!
scenes.titleZh: 祝你有玉米般美好的一天！
scenes.practice: Give a cheerful wish, echo a surprising phrase, and explain a pun. Corntastic combines corn and fantastic; it is wordplay, not a standard adjective.
scenes.editNote: Continuous source interval. Preserve the family laughter and the child’s What? before the explanation. No song remix or generated speech.

verification.method: Source frames, original audio/captions, and independent base.en/small.en recognition of uncut 55–74-second context.
verification.dialogue: Corrected the earlier draft guys to really using original automatic captions and independent recognition. Burned-in captions paraphrase that word. The pun is about corn, not the recognizers’ pineapple/cone substitutions.
verification.cut: Starts after dollar; last corn ends around 67.7, with release/laughter retained until 71.4. Next sentence starts after 72.0. No generated speech.
verification.roles: Tariq gives the wish and explanation. Julian echoes the wish. The woman’s laughter remains in the original mix.

lines.speaker: Tariq
lines.text: I hope you really have a corntastic day!
lines.hint: 祝你们有玉米般美好的一天！这里把 corn 和 fantastic 合成一个双关词。

lines.speaker: Tariq
lines.text: What? It's just a pun about corn!
lines.hint: 怎么了？这只是一个关于玉米的双关语！

scenes.contentNotes: Original interview, not the song remix. Corntastic is a playful blend of corn and fantastic, not standard vocabulary. Original child performance; source reuse rights remain unconfirmed. Adult prototype testing only.

scenes.title: Apparently, you get dizzy!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Tell me about the ride. What did you think about the ride?
lines.hint: 说说这个游乐项目吧，你觉得怎么样？

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: Because apparently you're spinning around, and apparently every time you get dizzy.
lines.hint: 因为显然你会转来转去，而且显然每次都会晕。

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: That's all you do is get dizzy.

scenes.contentNotes: Original spontaneous interview; repetition and nonstandard phrasing are preserved as a performance, not a grammar model. No child age-rating claim. The other child’s later television remark starts after this continuous excerpt.
scenes.practice: Ask and answer questions about an experience; practise excitement and apparently.

verification.method: Source frames and independent base.en/small.en recognition on uncut 22–54 seconds.
verification.roles: Sofia Ojeda asks the off-screen questions, including Yeah?; Noah answers. The other child’s later television line is outside this cut.
verification.cut: Begins after the preceding Powerball answer. Retains Noah’s final Yeah and its release; ends before the other child starts the next line around 39.66.

scenes.title: Emotional damage!

lines.speaker: Aunty
lines.text: Steven, when you get so fat?
lines.hint: 史蒂文，你什么时候变得这么胖了？这是一句不礼貌的讽刺台词。

lines.speaker: Steven
lines.text: You probably could just hold down the block button.
lines.hint: 你也许只要一直按住格挡键就行了。

scenes.contentNotes: A staged comedy sketch with an insulting body comment and stereotyped characters; adult prototype material. Aunty’s nonstandard question is preserved from the performance, not taught as polite/standard English. Therapy is part of the joke, not health advice.
scenes.practice: Perform the famous reaction, then give a practical suggestion using probably could.

verification.method: Source frames, original audio/automatic captions, independent base.en/small.en recognition, and cross-check of the quoted Aunty line against published source analyses.
verification.roles: Aunty gives the off-screen game taunt; the dad reacts and asks about therapy; Steven in the green shirt gives the block-button suggestion. Aunty is retained as non-practice support because this short insulting line offers little useful practice.
verification.cut: Begins after dad’s preceding action line. Final button ends around 72.78; the cut retains its release and stops before Aunty restarts around 73.08. Prompts stop before the next speaker.

scenes.contentNotes: Original 2007 broadcast, not the 2023 promotional recreation. Zombie face paint may unsettle some viewers. Preserve the unexpected answer; it is a comic non sequitur rather than a recommended interview response. Adult prototype; source reuse permission unconfirmed.

verification.method: Uncut source frames and independent small.en recognition; CTC alignment of final authored dialogue.

verification.cut: The original 17-second archive is the uncut comparison source. Zombie finishes around 12.64; release retained to 13.08, before Good times begins around 13.38. The archive’s final broadcast sentence is outside the selected exchange.
